name: Fibonacci M944P696

conventions.node_rule: Native residues divisible by 3, including zero; preserves the approved M6/M9/M12 reference selection. Additional regular formations of all native values are catalogued separately.

beta.endpoint_rule: Exclude endpoints, include wraparound; raw residues used for sums. Empty interiors sum to zero.

epsilon_status: Null: no tested regular six-node reference traversal contains only 3, 6 and 9 with all three present.

geometry_summary.scope: Shapes in the primary Gamma node set (native residues divisible by 3, including zero). All regular polygons on the period circle are catalogued separately with their native values; their existence alone is a property of the plotting grid.
geometry_summary.epsilon_rule: A regular six-node formation must support the reference unicursal route through only 3, 6 and 9, containing all three. Rotations and reflections of the route are tested; reversed or cyclically shifted traversals are deduplicated.

background_literature.scope: Shared background literature for the initial OXTR research programme across M1–M1001. Studies of related mechanisms in other systems provide context for investigation.

verification.scope: Native period, sequences, regular polygon index spacing and reference Epsilon routes; no physical or biological validation.
verification.wolfram_scope: Native Pisano period; complete Alpha, primary Gamma indices, Beta interval sums and residues, primary equilateral-triangle and hexagon indices. Independent integer Fibonacci evaluation and SHA-256 comparisons. Extended catalogue, Chevron and native/cycle-based Epsilon are Python-checked.

reduction_to_m9.research_question: Does the shared M9 pattern have shared biological relevance, or does native-modulus complexity change it? Unassessed: requires peer-reviewed evidence, in silico modelling (including proposed CUDA/CUDA-Q work), and appropriate experimental validation. No spatial-dimension claim or WSS score follows from this arithmetic match.

epsilon_m9_comparison.orientation: clockwise from north; fixed M9 route and starting phase
epsilon_m9_comparison.reason: Reference geometry exists, but the reduced traversal does not equal 9–3–6–9–3–6–9.
epsilon_m9_comparison.scope: Tests the fixed north-oriented M9 path on the full native period circle; does not fold the period or rotate/reverse the values to force a match.

epsilon_assessment.absence_reason: No tested six-node formation contains only 3, 6 and 9 with all three present.

research_register.title: First Principles Genomics — research register
research_register.scope: Shared background literature for the initial OXTR research programme across M1–M1001. Studies of related mechanisms in other systems provide context for investigation.
research_register.hypothesis: The Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Epsilon sequences of M9P24 may offer useful descriptions of biological timing, cellular division and molecular organisation in the context of OXTR. Bioinformatics and in silico modelling provide the planned means of investigation.
research_register.interpretation: Publication findings describe their original experimental systems. Links from Atlas records identify shared reading; a sequence-to-biology correspondence remains open for assessment.
research_register.hero_selection: Four lead references within the fourteen unique publications, one for each theme.

wss.meaning: Future assessment of relevance to individual Atlas records. Publication trust scores remain separate from WSS.

appraisal_method.label: Provisional editorial trust
appraisal_method.purpose: Prioritise closer reading of reported findings. This is an editorial assessment, without calibration or independent peer review.

criteria.3: Controlled mechanistic test or quantitative prediction tested by manipulation
Main text, relevant methods/results and captions reviewed

appraisal_method.independent_replication_appraisal: Not yet completed for this collection
appraisal_method.citation_policy: Crossref cited-by counts are a dated contextual snapshot and contribute no points. Coverage depends on deposited references. Unavailable counts remain null.
appraisal_method.journal_policy: Journal reputation and impact factor contribute no points.
appraisal_method.jadad_policy: Jadad concerns reporting of randomised clinical trials. It is not applicable to these fourteen study designs; no numeric Jadad score is assigned.

publications.title: Reconstitution of circadian oscillation of cyanobacterial KaiC phosphorylation in vitro
publications.author: Nakajima et al.
publications.methods: Purified cyanobacterial clock proteins; biochemical reconstitution
publications.finding: KaiA, KaiB, KaiC and ATP supported self-sustaining phosphorylation oscillation. Temperature compensation and agreement between mutant periods in vitro and in vivo strengthened the biological interpretation.
publications.relevance: direct evidence for a molecular timing mechanism; a broad Alpha reference independent of OXTR.
publications.limit: biochemical reconstruction is more informative about mechanism than visual analogy. It is a cyanobacterial system, not a mammalian receptor study, and does not support a universal exact 24-hour period or M9 correspondence.
publications.access: primary abstract and publication metadata. Replication and detailed methods require full-text appraisal before a formal quality rating.
publications.scoreReason: Molecular reconstitution tests a timing mechanism; appraisal currently covers the abstract and metadata.
publications.crossrefTitle: Reconstitution of Circadian Oscillation of Cyanobacterial KaiC Phosphorylation in Vitro

publications.title: Phase locking and multiple oscillating attractors for the coupled mammalian clock and cell cycle
publications.author: Feillet et al.
publications.methods: Mouse fibroblasts; live-cell imaging and modelling
publications.finding: live imaging of proliferating mouse fibroblasts, combined with modelling, identified phase locking and additional clock states under different conditions.
publications.relevance: direct support for studying relationships between biological cycles; connects the Alpha and Beta research themes without making them equivalent.
publications.limit: single-cell observations support the dynamical interpretation. Culture conditions and synchronisation matter, and related cells are not automatically independent replicates. No modular doubling or Atlas geometry was tested.
publications.access: primary abstract and selected results, including period distributions. A phase-space representation is not evidence of a physical toroidal cell structure.
publications.scoreReason: Live-cell observations and modelling provide complementary evidence for phase locking; selected results appraised.
publications.crossrefTitle: Phase locking and multiple oscillating attractors for the coupled mammalian clock and cell cycle

publications.title: Interaction between time-of-day and oxytocin efficacy in mice and humans with and without gestational diabetes
publications.author: Duong et al.
publications.methods: Mouse genetics; human cells; retrospective human records
publications.finding: mouse experiments support BMAL1 regulation of Oxtr and time-dependent oxytocin responsiveness. Human myometrial-cell experiments and records from 2,367 patients add distinct translational observations.
publications.relevance: a direct OXTR connection to the Alpha theme.
publications.limit: genetic perturbation and promoter experiments strengthen mechanism. Animal, cell and retrospective components need separate appraisal; the human observations can be confounded. Uterine findings do not establish effects in brain tissue.
publications.access: final publication abstract and selected full-text results. The 2024 preprint is superseded for this register and is not counted as another study.
publications.scoreReason: Genetic and promoter experiments support mechanism; the human observational component has separate confounding limits.
publications.crossrefTitle: Interaction between time-of-day and oxytocin efficacy in mice and humans with and without gestational diabetes

publications.title: Cryptochromes mediate rhythmic repression of the glucocorticoid receptor
publications.author: Lamia et al.
publications.methods: Mouse cells and mice; genetic and biochemical experiments
publications.finding: Cry1/Cry2 interacted with the glucocorticoid receptor and altered glucocorticoid-responsive transcription in mouse cells, with related metabolic phenotypes in mice.
publications.relevance: direct circadian–receptor evidence provides a natural NR3C1 example beyond oxytocin.
publications.limit: molecular interactions, genetic perturbations and physiological observations complement one another. Multiple pathways change in knockout animals; the results do not isolate a universal geometric explanation or establish human clinical effects.
publications.access: primary abstract and selected experimental/results text. NR3C1 identifies the receptor target; the principal genetic perturbations here involved cryptochromes.
publications.scoreReason: Genetic perturbations, molecular interactions and physiological measurements support the reported mechanism.
publications.crossrefTitle: Cryptochromes mediate rhythmic repression of the glucocorticoid receptor

publications.title: Experimental and theoretical study of mitotic spindle orientation
publications.author: Théry et al.
publications.methods: Human HeLa cells; controlled adhesion geometry and modelling
publications.finding: controlled adhesion patterns in human HeLa cells, combined with a physical model, accounted for spindle-orientation distributions across different microenvironment geometries.
publications.relevance: direct evidence that geometry is a meaningful biological variable; supports interest in the Beta/division theme and related shape families.
publications.limit: manipulation of the cell environment offers more than an observational resemblance. The model uses specific force assumptions and a transformed cell line. Division orientation is distinct from division rate, population doubling or a Fibonacci sequence.
publications.access: publisher abstract and figure descriptions. Full methods and sample accounting remain to be appraised.
publications.scoreReason: Controlled adhesion geometry tests a quantitative model; full methods and sample accounting remain open for appraisal.
publications.crossrefTitle: Experimental and theoretical study of mitotic spindle orientation

publications.title: Oxytocin promotes epicardial cell activation and heart regeneration after cardiac injury
publications.author: Wasserman et al.
publications.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
publications.methods: Human stem-cell-derived epicardial cells and zebrafish
publications.finding: OXT promoted activation and proliferation-related outcomes in human stem-cell-derived epicardial cells; OXTR knockdown removed the response. Zebrafish experiments supplied a separate regeneration context.
publications.relevance: a direct OXTR-related example for the Beta research theme.
publications.limit: receptor knockdown strengthens causal interpretation within the model. Check independent cell lines and differentiation batches; images are subsamples, not donors. Cultured epicardial cells and fish regeneration do not establish regeneration of adult human hearts.
publications.access: primary full-text methods/results and relevant figure captions, including OXTR knockdown and proliferation measurements.
publications.scoreReason: Receptor knockdown provides a mechanistic test alongside cell and zebrafish experiments; methods and results appraised.
publications.crossrefTitle: Oxytocin promotes epicardial cell activation and heart regeneration after cardiac injury

publications.title: Oxytocin stimulates hippocampal neurogenesis via oxytocin receptor expressed in CA3 pyramidal neurons
publications.author: Lin et al.
publications.finding: conditional Oxtr deletion in mouse hippocampal excitatory neurons affected survival and maturation of newly generated neurons, while measured progenitor proliferation and early differentiation were unchanged.
publications.relevance: direct evidence that the biological outcome must be named precisely. It bounds generalisations from E06 without contradicting a different tissue-specific finding.
publications.limit: conditional genetics help localise the process. Appraise cell-type specificity, blinding and precision; an unchanged measured outcome does not prove absence of every possible effect.
publications.access: primary results/discussion. Retained deliberately to avoid presenting all OXTR growth-related findings as evidence of duplication.
publications.scoreReason: Conditional genetics and cell-outcome measurements distinguish survival from proliferation in this mouse system.
publications.crossrefTitle: Oxytocin stimulates hippocampal neurogenesis via oxytocin receptor expressed in CA3 pyramidal neurons

publications.title: Structural basis for the activation and ligand recognition of the human oxytocin receptor
publications.author: Waltenspühl et al.
publications.methods: Engineered human receptor complex; cryo-EM and functional assays
publications.finding: cryo-EM at 3.2 Å and functional experiments characterised OXT recognition and receptor activation. All nine peptide residues participate in binding.
publications.relevance: a direct structural foundation for Gamma's molecular-recognition theme; useful context, but not confirmation, for the OXT-specific Epsilon proposal.
publications.limit: structure–function comparisons strengthen interpretation. Receptor stabilisation and an engineered G protein affect generalisation. The six-residue disulfide loop is not itself an aromatic hexagon; the reported contacts do not establish an Epsilon trajectory.
publications.access: full primary article main text, receptor-engineering description and functional-assay captions. No new molecular analysis performed.
publications.scoreReason: Structural observations and functional residue tests provide complementary evidence; main text and assay descriptions appraised.
publications.crossrefTitle: Structural basis for the activation and ligand recognition of the human oxytocin receptor

publications.title: X-ray structures and mechanism of the human serotonin transporter
publications.author: Coleman, Green & Gouaux
publications.methods: Engineered human serotonin transporter; crystallography and assays
publications.finding: structures of human SERT bound to antidepressants identified central and allosteric binding sites and explained aspects of inhibitor recognition.
publications.relevance: direct structural evidence broadens Gamma beyond OXTR to SLC6A4.
publications.limit: structural and binding/transport measurements are complementary. Thermostabilised constructs were used; the ts3 construct had no detectable transport activity. Results describe particular inhibitor-bound conformations rather than every physiological state.
publications.access: publisher abstract and selected primary methods/results. These data concern the protein product and ligand recognition, not regulation of SLC6A4 gene expression.
publications.scoreReason: Structures and functional measurements complement one another; engineered constructs constrain interpretation.
publications.crossrefTitle: X-ray structures and mechanism of the human serotonin transporter

publications.title: Structure of a D2 dopamine receptor–G-protein complex in a lipid membrane
publications.author: Yin et al.
publications.methods: Engineered human DRD2 complex in a lipid membrane; cryo-EM
publications.finding: cryo-EM characterised an agonist-bound DRD2–Gi complex within a reconstituted phospholipid membrane, identifying receptor, G-protein and lipid interactions.
publications.relevance: direct evidence for the structural context of molecular recognition; another Gamma hero example.
publications.limit: including a lipid environment improves contextual relevance relative to isolated detergent structures. The receptor complex is engineered and ligand-bound; it does not represent every receptor state or establish clinical outcomes.
publications.access: primary abstract and selected full-text structural results, with deposited structural metadata checked. No geometric correspondence to the Atlas was analysed.
publications.scoreReason: A membrane-reconstituted structural observation provides a defined molecular state; independent functional validation needs fuller appraisal.
publications.crossrefTitle: Structure of a D2 dopamine receptor–G-protein complex in a lipid membrane

publications.title: Assembly of a π–π stack of ligands in the binding site of an acetylcholine-binding protein
publications.author: Stornaiuolo et al.
publications.methods: Molluscan binding protein; crystallography and solution assays
publications.finding: an Aplysia acetylcholine-binding protein accommodated a stack of three aromatic ligands. Solution binding measurements supported the structural observation.
publications.relevance: direct experimental support for π-stacking as a molecular-recognition phenomenon; an Epsilon reference that does not depend on OXTR.
publications.limit: crystallography, mutagenesis and solution assays help address crystallographic-artifact concerns. This soluble molluscan protein is a model for receptor ligand-binding domains, not a complete human receptor. Neither the three-ligand count nor the stacked geometry establishes the Atlas traversal.
publications.access: full primary main text, including solution validation and scope of the receptor model.
publications.scoreReason: Structures, mutagenesis and solution assays support the binding interpretation; full main text appraised.
publications.crossrefTitle: Assembly of a π–π stack of ligands in the binding site of an acetylcholine-binding protein

publications.title: Targeted disruption of pi–pi stacking in Malaysian banana lectin reduces mitogenicity while preserving antiviral activity
publications.author: Covés-Datson et al.
publications.methods: Engineered plant lectin; structures and cellular assays
publications.finding: an F84T mutation disrupted aromatic stacking in Malay BanLec, reduced mitogenic activity and retained antiviral activity in the studied assays.
publications.relevance: a direct structure–function example for Epsilon; also connects molecular interactions with proliferation as a biological outcome.
publications.limit: structural checks and functional comparisons strengthen the rationale. Mutation can change several properties simultaneously, so this is not a pure isolation of one energetic contribution. Plant-lectin effects do not establish OXTR behaviour or clinical benefit.
publications.access: primary abstract and main structural/results sections. Published in 2021 despite “2020” appearing within the DOI.
publications.scoreReason: Targeted mutation and structural / cellular comparisons connect aromatic organisation with biological outcomes.
publications.crossrefTitle: Targeted disruption of pi–pi stacking in Malaysian banana lectin reduces mitogenicity while preserving antiviral activity

publications.title: Reconstruction of molecular orbital densities from photoemission data
publications.author: Puschnig et al.
publications.methods: Organic molecular films; photoemission and calculations
publications.finding: photoemission measurements and Fourier reconstruction yielded orbital-density distributions for pentacene films and p-sexiphenyl monolayers, compared with density-functional calculations.
publications.relevance: direct physics evidence for studying spatial electronic structure; contextual to the valence-electron theme and more distant from biological significance.
publications.limit: comparison of measurement and theory is valuable. Reconstruction is model-dependent and the samples are non-living materials. Orbital densities are not classical electron orbits or evidence of unicursal electron motion.
publications.access: primary abstract and metadata. No biological role, creation-of-life claim or numeric WSS assignment follows from this paper.
publications.scoreReason: Measurement and reconstruction are compared with calculations; current appraisal is abstract-level.
publications.crossrefTitle: Reconstruction of Molecular Orbital Densities from Photoemission Data

publications.title: CD38 is critical for social behaviour by regulating oxytocin secretion
publications.author: Jin et al.
publications.methods: Mice; Cd38 knockout and rescue experiments
publications.finding: Cd38-knockout mice showed altered oxytocin secretion and behavioural phenotypes. Oxytocin replacement or hypothalamic delivery of human CD38 rescued selected outcomes.
publications.relevance: direct support for CD38 involvement in the oxytocin system. Retained as supporting hero context without forcing it into a particular sequence family.
publications.limit: knockout plus rescue strengthens causal interpretation in mice. Global deletion, behavioural measurement and human translation require careful appraisal. This concerns secretion, not proof of OXTR-expression regulation or geometric correspondence.
publications.access: primary abstract and figure descriptions. Full methods are needed before formal risk-of-bias grading.
publications.scoreReason: Knockout and rescue experiments test the secretion mechanism; full methods remain open for appraisal.
publications.crossrefTitle: CD38 is critical for social behaviour by regulating oxytocin secretion

formation_interval_encoding.rule: For each formation interval, walk clockwise from from_index + 1 to to_index, excluding both endpoints and wrapping modulo P. Read values from alpha.residues. Endpoints, sum and residue are retained.
